newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: EMI's Lamfalussy - no threat to ECB independence.
newsitem.headline: EMI's Lamfalussy - no threat to ECB independence.

text.p: European Monetary Institute president Alexandre Lamfalussy said on Monday he did not see any risk to the independence of the future European central bank even after Bonn's controversial plan to revalue Bundesbank gold reserves.

Asked if he saw a risk to the independence of the ECB from the project, which the Bundesbank has said endangers its autonomy, Lamfalussy said, "Not at all. I see no risk whatsoever to the independence of the European central bank."
Lamfalussy declined further comment on the gold revaluation plan saying that he had views on the subject but no time to elaborate on them.
Lamfalussy was speaking to reporters on the fringes of the International Monetary Conference meting in Interlaken.
Bonn has proposed revaluing the Bundesbank's assets with a view to transferring an extraordinary profit to the government this year and next.
